Judgment

1. Vide this judgment, this court shall dispose of the revision petition u/s 397 of Cr.P.C. against the impugned order dated 21- 12-2023 passed by the court of Ms. Arushi Parwal, Ld. MM (Mahila Court-02), NE Distt, KKD, Delhi in CC no. 227/16 titled State Vs. Gaurav Teotia & Ors.

sentences.text: In case FIR no. 1333/14, PS Gokulpuri whereby the Ld. Trial Court has framed charges against respondent no. 2 to 4 for the offences punishable u/s 498A/34 of IPC.

In addition, respondents no. 2 and 4 were also charged for the offence punishable u/s 406/34 of IPC.
2.
The facts in brief are that the revisionist got married with respondent no. 2 on 27-11-2009 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.

It is claimed by the revisionist that during the marriage, the parents of revisionist had incurred substantial amount, however, respondent no. 2 as well as other in-laws were not happy with the gifts and articles presented in the marriage.
They used to commit cruelty upon the revisionist for bringing insufficient dowry articles.

It is further alleged that respondent no.
2 used to compel the revisionist to have unnatural acts and when the revisionist reported about the same to her mother-in- law, she did not pay any heed.

Prior to the marriage, the respondent no. 2 represented himself to be in good job as an engineer in Bangalore and earning more than Rs.
50,000/- per month, but later on after marriage it was found that he was not an engineer.

sentences.text: Various other instances have been revealed in the complaint wherein the revisionist was subjected to cruelty.
A complaint was initially filed in CAW Cell, which after inquiry, culminated in registration of FIR.
Since the respondents were cooperating in the investigation, they were not arrested.
After necessary formalities, chargesheet was filed in the court.
3. Vide order dated 21-12-2023, Ld. Trial Court has framed charges against respondent no. 2 to 4 for the offences punishable u/s 498A/34 of IPC.
Respondents no. 2 and 4 were also charged for the offence punishable u/s 406/34 of IPC.

4. Feeling aggrieved by the said order, the revisionist has preferred the present revision petition on the following grounds:-
(a) The Ld. Trial has failed to take into consideration the allegations pertaining to offence punishable u/s 406 of IPC have also been levelled against respondent no. 3 as well, as reflected from statement u/s 161 of Cr.P.C of mother of revisionist namely Santosh.

(b) Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that specific allegations pertaining to commission of offence punishable u/s 377 of IPC have been levelled by the revisionist in para no. 5 of the complaint.
(c) The allegations levelled in para no. 7 of the complaint indicates that respondent no. 2 has committed offence punishable u/s 417 of IPC as well.
(d) Ld. Trial has failed to consider the written submissions, forwarded by ld. APP for State, which were filed on behalf of revisionist.

5. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondents have vehemently denied all the infirmities in the impugned order pointed out by the revisionist and stated that Ld. Trial Court has passed a well reasoned order and no interference in the said order is called for.
6. I have heard Ld. Counsel for revisionist, Ld. Counsel for respondents, Ld. Addl. PP for State and have perused the trial court record.

7. It is noted that in para no. 5 of the complaint, it is stated that respondent no. 2 herein also used to compel the revisionist to have unnatural acts and whenever the revisionist declined his request, he used to beat her mercilessly.
It is pertinent to note that Section 377 of IPC punishes acts of unnatural intercourse and not all acts.

Section 377 of IPC reads as under:

sentences.text: Unnatural offences.--Whoever voluntarily has carnal intercourse against the order of nature with any man, woman or animal, shall be punished with 2[imprisonment for life], or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
In view of plain reading of Section 377 of IPC, in the opinion of this court, Section 377 of IPC is not attracted in the present case.

8. As far as allegations of respondent no. 2 misrepresenting the revisionist that he was an engineer in Bangalore is concerned, it is noted that revisionist has nowhere specified as to when she got to know that respondent no. 2 was not an engineer.
Admittedly, the revisionist got married in the year 2009 and the present complaint was filed in the year 2014.
Section 417 of IPC is punishable with imprisonment upto one year only.
Thus, invoking of Section 417 of IPC, as pressed, cannot be done being barred by prescribed period of limitation as per Cr.P.C.
Thus, in the opinion of this court, even Section 417 of IPC is not attracted against respondent no. 2, as alleged.

9. As far as invoking of section 406 of IPC is concerned, this court agrees with the submissions of Ld. Counsel for revisionist that said charge has been framed on the basis of statement of Smt.
Santosh, mother of revisionist wherein she had stated that parents of respondent no. 2 had put entire jewellery of revisionist in bank locker.
Thus, in the opinion of this court, Ld. Trial court has erred in not framing charge for the offence punishable u/s 406 of IPC against respondent no. 3.

Accordingly, the impugned order dated 21-12-2023 is partly set aside and Ld. Trial Court is directed to frame charge for the offence punishable u/s 406 of IPC against respondent no. 3 Mangeram Teotia as well.
The revision petition stands partly allowed.
Trial Court record be segregated and returned to the Ld. Trial Court with copy of this judgment and thereafter, revision file be consigned to Record Room.
